Compare smoothing schemes on one dataset

Source: R/smoothing.R
compare_smoothing.Rd

compare_smoothing() fits a tree under each of several smoothing schemes, with every other setting held fixed, and reports one row per scheme with the size of the tree and its in-sample perplexity. Given an already fitted tree, it re-smooths that tree under each scheme instead, which keeps its contexts, for example after pruning.

The number of contexts is the same for every scheme, because smoothing changes probabilities, not which contexts exist. In-sample perplexity favors schemes that stay close to the observed proportions and therefore is not a criterion for choosing one; tune_tree() compares schemes on held-out data. See smooth_tree() for the definitions of the schemes.

Usage

compare_smoothing(
  data,
  smoothing = c("floor", "laplace", "kneser_ney", "witten_bell", "jelinek_mercer"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Sequences in any form accepted by context_tree(), fitted afresh under each scheme, or a fitted transitiontrees, re-smoothed under each scheme.

smoothing

Names of the schemes to compare. Default all five: "floor", "laplace", "kneser_ney", "witten_bell", "jelinek_mercer", each with its default hyperparameters.

...

Further arguments to context_tree(), such as max_depth and min_count, held fixed across schemes. Not used when data is a fitted tree.

Value

A data.frame with one row per scheme, in the order of smoothing, and columns smoothing, n_nodes (number of contexts) and perplexity (in-sample).

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when smoothing is not a non-empty character vector of known methods, or when data cannot be fitted (see context_tree()).

References

Chen, S. F., & Goodman, J. (1999). An empirical study of smoothing techniques for language modeling. Computer Speech and Language, 13(4), 359-393. doi:10.1006/csla.1999.0128

See also

smooth_tree() for the schemes; tune_tree() for cross-validated selection; compare_pruning() for the analogous comparison of pruning criteria.

Examples

compare_smoothing(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
#>        smoothing n_nodes perplexity
#> 1          floor      38   2.244394
#> 2        laplace      38   2.250477
#> 3     kneser_ney      38   2.249175
#> 4    witten_bell      38   2.245722
#> 5 jelinek_mercer      38   2.281600
compare_smoothing(trajectories, smoothing = c("floor", "kneser_ney"),
                  max_depth = 2, min_count = 10)
#>    smoothing n_nodes perplexity
#> 1      floor      13   2.310147
#> 2 kneser_ney      13   2.310592
